title_content.content: Sensing-Communication Co-Design for UAV Swarm-Assisted Vehicular Network in Perspective of Doppler

paragraph_content.content: Qian Zhu , Rongke Liu , Senior Member, IEEE, Zijie Wang , Qirui Liu , Graduate Student Member, IEEE, and Changwen Chen , Fellow, IEEE

Abstract—Utilizing the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm to realize sensing and communication for ground vehicles (GVs) has been envisioned as a promising technology in harsh environments. Previous research in vehicular networks has ignored or assumed perfect elimination of Doppler, resulting in unstable or impractical dynamic system models. However, Doppler is essential for multidimensional sensing, especially for velocity estimation, but it may lead to loss of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in communication. In this case, to achieve satisfying sensing and communication performance simultaneously, we propose a sensing-communication co-design scheme for UAV swarm-assisted vehicular networks in perspective of Doppler. We first establish the mathematical models for the effect of Doppler on communication and sensing respectively. Then we analyze the influence of UAVs link selection on GV sensing-communication performance. Based on this framework, we aim to minimize the GVs’ maximum Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for sensing estimates with an SNR loss constraint to make a sensing-communication performance trade-off. Finally, an efficient differential evolution (DE)-based algorithm is developed to find a sub-optimal solution for this complicated non-convex problem. Numerical results demonstrate the validity and superiority of our co-design scheme. Compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our scheme can not only improve the sensing accuracy by more than 30% while ensuring communication, but also outperform over 20% in communication without sacrificing sensing capacity.
Index Terms—Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm, sensingcommunication co-design, doppler, cramer-rao lower bound (CRLB).

W ITH the in-depth promotion and commercialization ofthe fifth generation (5G) wireless networks, it is fore- the fifth generation (5G) wireless networks, it is foreseeable that the booming burgeon of future sixth generation (6G) is irresistible [1]. 5G presents a new paradigm to provide massive ubiquitous connectivity, in which the vehicle-toeverything (V2X) technology has been expected to substantially promote public living standards [2], [3], [4], [5]. However, these intelligent vehicle networks are often deployed in harsh network environments, such as urban canyons and isolated areas, where global navigation satellite system (GNSS) and other traditional positioning technologies may suffer serious performance degradation due to continual non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation [6], [7] and available anchor nodes with imperfect geometry [8], [9]. In this case, UAVs, with their advantages of high mobility and flexible deployment, have been envisioned as a promising solution to assist ground vehicles (GVs) to achieve network connection service, making up for the deficiency of GNSS [10], [11]. In addition, it is precisely for these reasons that UAVs have attracted widespread attention in both academia and industry, and may help provide a new quintessence for 6G vehicle networks [12], [13].

Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is considered a crucial and popular research interest in 6G era, where sensing and communication are forming a virtuous circle of mutual benefit [14], [15], [16]. With numerous sensing-communication applications springing up, it requires improving the performance of various networks to meet the demand of realizing multiple functions simultaneously. Nevertheless, in the existing research on UAV-assisted vehicle networks, the main functions such as location navigation and data communication are commonly designed separately [17]. In addition, the sensing performance of 6G vehicle networks not only includes the common position sensing, but also focus on the velocity sensing and other capabilities, which could realize the sensing dimensions increase and apply to more innovative sensing scenarios, such as coarsegrained indoor positioning [18], activity recognition [19] and even augmented reality [20].

Recently, many studies have shown that considering the collaboration of sensing and communication in the early stage of system design, namely sensing-communication co-design, can help improve system properties or resource efficiency, thus solving the above problems [21], [22]. In the scenario of [23], vehicle motion prediction based on radar perception is used to assist in receiving downlink communication signals. However, the performance metrics of these two functionalities are separate, which makes it impossible to compare them under a unified theoretical framework. The collaborative design of communication and control for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) networks is introducted in [24], [25], both of which design resource scheduling algorithm to ensure the stability of vehicle communication. In these two studies, the sensing errors of vehicles are perfectly assumed to be nonexistent, which is unrealistic in the actual situation. The authors in [26] and [27] study the control-aware communication to promote the resource utilization efficiency of wireless systems, but their research focuses on system control and resource utilization rather than measuring the ability to perform various tasks. These efforts contribute to understanding the mechanism behind the sensing-communication co-design. Unfortunately, there is still a lack of a theoretical framework to specify the trade-off between communication and sensing.

paragraph_content.content: As two typical sensing functionalities, velocity measurement and localization occupy the equal important status in UAVassisted vehicular networks. Many literatures have studied the positioning performance of UAV-assisted system by typical positioning methods such as Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) or Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDOA) [28], [29], [30], but they only consider the static deployment of UAVs without involving the dynamic scene and the field of velocity perception, resulting in limited application scope. Doppler is an indispensable topic in velocity sensing, and it widely exists in dynamic vehicle networks under high relative motion scenario [31], [32]. In existing studies, Doppler shift in the channel is often either ignored for convenience or assumed to have been perfectly eliminated by relevant techniques for the communication purpose [33], [34], [35]. However, in the sensing domain, by introducing FDOA, it is equivalent to adding a constraint to TDOA, which can not only estimate the target velocity, but also improve its position accuracy [36], [37]. Combined with the above research, it can be seen that at present, the research on communication and sensing of Doppler is parallel, and the two have almost no intersection. Although the respective influence of Doppler on communication and sensing is self-evident, its unified performance index and theoretical framework have not been clearly defined so far, making it still an open issue.

Combined with the above considerations, we shall focus particularly on the establishment of a theoretical framework for sensing-communication co-design, with Doppler as the point of penetration. Besides, The above research point can also provide theoretical support for future vehicle network design meeting more requirements simultaneously, which also has tremendous potential in the aspect of promoting sensing accuracy while guaranteeing communication capability. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to probe into both the sensing and communication co-design for UAV-assisted vehicle network from the perspective of Doppler. In the longer term, the framework of sensing-communication co-design may be applied to the integration of vehicles and other smart devices in the future vehicle networks [38], which also be expected to bring a new paradigm for the key technology of the future wireless networks design.

In this article, a Doppler-oriented sensing-communication co-design scheme is proposed to improve the sensing accuracy of UAV-assisted vehicle networks while ensuring GVs’ communication requirements. To further evaluate the performance of the proposed design, we do comparison simulations with benchmark methods at different functional levels, including sensing and communication aspects respectively. In particular, the communication and sensing metrics derived from Doppler respectively are applied to the optimization problem of the proposed framework. Specifically, the main contributions of our research can be elaborated on as follows.

item_content.content: 1) We consider a practical UAV swarm-assisted vehicle network consisting of multiple low-altitude UAVs and a terrestrial base station (BS) to provide network connectivity services for GVs in city canyon environments, which is a realistic dynamic three-dimensional (3-D) time slice with instantaneous coordinates and velocity vectors.
2) We take the Doppler in the network UAV-GV links as the breakthrough point and derive the mathematical models of the influence on the communication and sensing respectively.
3) We use two Doppler-based performance indicators obtained in 2) to construct the theoretical framework of sensing-communication trade-off and form related optimization problems.

4) We propose a differential evolution (DE)-based approach according to the optimization problem formed in 3). Further, we compare and analyze the proposed design with benchmark methods under the consideration of sensing and communication functional levels respectively.

paragraph_content.content: Numerical results demonstrate the proposed DE-based approach significantly enhances the sensing-communication capabilities in the UAV swarm-assisted vehicular network compared to the state-of-the-art methods. To some extent, the conclusion can be in turn serve as a recommendation for the practical use of future vehicle network.

The remainder of this article is organized as follows. The system model of the proposed UAV swarm-assisted vehicular network is introduced in Section II. Section III presents the Doppler-oriented sensing-communication framework and forms related optimization problems in detail. Section IV proposes the DE-based approach to slove the optimization problems in Section III. Section V provides numerical results to demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed algorithm in sensing-communication performance trade-off. Finally, the concluding remarks are drawn in Section VI.

paragraph_content.content: In this article, as shown in Fig. 1, we consider a typical urban canyon scenario, where multiple GVs are waiting for services such as communication and sensing to be implemented utilizing aerial UAV swarm. In such scenario, conventional technologies such as GNSS systems and terrestrial cellular-based positioning fail to meet GVs’ location requirements due to building blockage [39]. The considered UAV swarm-assisted vehicular network consists of M moving low-altitude UAV platforms as aerial anchor nodes and K moving GVs. As an aerial reference station, ARS is directly connected with the BSs to achieve accurate self-positioning. In addition, ARS can assist the UAV swarm to achieve self-positioning through providing absolute measurements, which can cover a larger signal blind to provide sensing-communication services for multiple GVs. In this article, we propose a generic analytical framework for UAV swarm-assisted vehicular networks in urban canyon areas, where the UAVs have the mission of providing sensing and communication services concurrently for GVs. Unlike prior research, this article focuses on the co-design between the sensing and communication from a Doppler perspective to meet
\mathrm { G V s } ^ { \prime }
communication requirements while achieving high sensing accuracy. Specifically, we formulated an optimization problem to minimize the GVs’ maximum CRLB with a specific
D n f

constraint by optimizing the UAVs links, aiming to consider the performance trade-off between sensing and communication. Due to the non-convexity of the optimization problem, we proposed a DE-based method with a local optimization of the UAV-GV links for finding a sub-optimal solution efficiently. The proposed scheme is evaluated on different benchmarks at various levels, which provides prerequisite value for our follow-up research on resource utilization and energy efficiency of UAV swarm under the proposed co-design scheme. Numerical results demonstrate the feasibility of our co-design scheme and the proposed DE-based method could further improve the sensing accuracy by exceed 30% compared with a random approach. In addition, the proposed method can enhance communication performance by more than 20% without sacrificing sensing accuracy.

Therefore, we foresee that Doppler-oriented sensingcommunication co-design scheme has the potential to play a vital role in the future vehicle networks. We hope this article could provide meaningful inspiration for UAV swarm-assisted vehicular applications, especially in the situations where both sensing and communication need to be considered.
